heroHeadline: PM Fils-Aimé Returns from Rome with IFAD Deal; 8 Killed by Savien Gang Near Saint-Marc as Artibonite Deteriorates Without GSF
heroSubtitle: Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé returned to Port-au-Prince on May 11, 2026, concluding his May 8–11 diplomatic mission to Rome and the Holy See. The mission yielded a new agricultural cooperation framework with IFAD (International Fund for Agricultural Development) targeting Haiti's rural recovery, and a partnership with the Community of Sant'Egidio — the Catholic peace-mediation organization — focused on youth empowerment and gang violence prevention given that an estimated 50% of active gang members are under 18. However, the PM's return was overshadowed by the deteriorating Artibonite security situation that continued on his watch: on May 9, the Savien gang killed 8 civilians and wounded 3 in Kafou Robert (fourth section of Saint-Marc), even though the municipality had imposed a nightly curfew just four days earlier. The Kafou Robert attack follows Viv Ansanm's destruction of the Marchand-Dessalines police station on May 7 and IOM's documentation of 4,419 additional IDPs from Petite-Rivière de l'Artibonite and Dessalines (May 2–7), bringing the national IDP total to 1.47M+. The core structural problem persists: the GSF advance force of ~545 personnel is exclusively focused on Port-au-Prince, leaving all of the Artibonite Department without international security support during a critical period when gangs are exploiting the security vacuum to consolidate Route Nationale 1 ahead of the harvest season. The full 5,500-person GSF will not reach operational capacity until fall–end 2026. On accountability: sentencing for the four Miami-convicted Moïse assassination defendants is scheduled for late summer 2026, though the higher-level masterminds remain unindicted. The August 30 election date remains increasingly in jeopardy — no electoral decree issued, no voter registration begun, and 23 communes still inaccessible. Haiti's 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains critically underfunded at approximately 20% of the $880 million required.
